works.abstract: Ingested foreign bodies are common occurrences in emergency departments, and imaging is often used to identify and locate the object. Radiolucent objects can be particularly challenging to identify with imaging, and careful scrutiny of images with knowledge of the ingested object’s appearance is required. We present a case of an accidentally ingested plastic fork in a patient with a history of bulimia nervosa. The plastic fork was retained in the patient’s stomach and duodenum for 3 years before the patient returned with complaints of abdominal pain and concern for cholecystitis. A subsequent CT examination showed evidence of the retained fork causing duodenal perforation. Review of CT images acquired 3 years earlier, initially interpreted as unremarkable, revealed subtle evidence of the ingested fork in the stomach on multiplanar reconstructions. Accidental foreign-body ingestion due to self-induced vomiting is not rare, and special attention must be given to foreign bodies that are not radiopaque. Additionally, such foreign bodies may persist in the gastrointestinal tract for years and manifest as acute abdomen long after the initial ingestion, highlighting the importance of not discounting prior foreign-body ingestion as a cause for current symptoms.
works.title: Duodenal Perforation due to a Swallowed Plastic Fork
